Rashi on Menachot 7a:10:2.hebrew: מכלי זה - ראה כלי מונח על גבי קרקע, וקאמר: כלי זה, אם של קודש (זה) היה, ראוי לקמיצה:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:10:2.english: From this vessel - [Avimi] saw a vessel resting on the ground and said: "This vessel, if it were sacred (this), would be fit for taking the handful."

Rashi on Menachot 7a:11:1.english: And how does one sanctify the handful - After the removal of the handful.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:12:1.hebrew: הוצרכתה ג' כהנים - שנים להגביה שני כלים, אחד שיקמוץ הימנו ואחד שנותן לתוכו, ושלישי קומץ. וכהן אחד אינו יכול להגביה שני הכלים, דאין עבודה בשמאל:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:12:1.english: You require three priests - Two [priests] to lift two vessels: one from which he will remove the handful, and one into which he places [it]; and a third [priest who] removes the handful. And one priest cannot lift the two vessels, as there is no [sacrificial] service with the left [hand].

Rashi on Menachot 7a:12:2.english: The daily offering - Thirteen priests merit [to participate] in it, [as taught] in Tractate Yoma in the second chapter (page 25a).

Rashi on Menachot 7a:13:1.english: This is the principle - It is a mishna.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:14:1.hebrew: סדר עבודות נקט - אותו שכהן אחד עושה זו אחר זו, אבל למניינא דכהנים לא נחתי:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:14:1.english: He cited the order of the services - That [order] which a single priest performs one after another, but he did not enter into the count of priests.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:15:1.english: What they do inside - In the Sanctuary.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:15:2.english: They enter - On the Shabbat day.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:15:3.hebrew: שני סדרי - של לחם הפנים, שתים המערכות, שש המערכת:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:15:3.english: Two arrangements - Of the shewbread: the two arrangements, six to an arrangement.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:1:1.hebrew: וקא פריך כי מהדר ליה לקומץ לדוכתיה ליקדוש וליפסול - דהא עבד מתן כלי, דמה לי כלי שרת זה ומה לי כלי שרת אחר:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:1:1.english: And [the Gemara] objects: When he returns the handful to its place, let it become sanctified and disqualified - For he has performed placement into a [service] vessel; for what difference does it make whether [it is] this service vessel or another service vessel?

Rashi on Menachot 7a:2:1.english: Only with intent - And [here] he did not place it there with the intention that it be sanctified.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:3:1.hebrew: שיקדשו פסולין - כגון אם קמץ זר ונותן לכלי, מהו שיקדישנו כלי להקטירו:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:3:1.english: That [service vessels] should sanctify disqualified [items] - For example, if a non-priest took the handful and placed [it] into a vessel, what is [the halakha as to whether] the vessel sanctifies it to be burned [on the altar]?

Rashi on Menachot 7a:3:2.hebrew: ליפסל - דקבעה ההוא כלי בקדושה כי יהביניה אדעתיה לקדושי, ולא מצי לאהדוריה תו לתוך השיריים, דהא פסול זה גמר לכולה עבודה:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:3:2.english: To be disqualified - For that vessel establishes it in sanctity when one placed it with the intention to sanctify [it], and one can no longer return it into the remainder [of the meal offering], since this disqualified [person] completed the entire service.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:4:1.hebrew: רב עמרם אמר - אפילו תימא שלא מדעת נמי מקדשין, והכא לא קדיש, שמחזירין לביסא גדושה, שאין מחזירה לתוך אויר הכלי, ואין הכלי מקדשו:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:4:1.english: Rav Amram said - Even if you say that [service vessels] also sanctify without intent, and here it did not become sanctified because they return [the handful] to a heaped bowl, as he does not return it into the airspace of the vessel, and the vessel does not sanctify it.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:4:2.english: A bowl - A service vessel in which they mix a meal offering.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:5:1.hebrew: ומקמץ היכי קמץ - תחילה כשקומץ מכלי זה, והלא גדוש הוא, וקמיצה מתוך הכלי בעינן, דכל דבר הטעון כלי אין חשוב כלי אלא תוכו:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:5:1.english: And taking the handful, how did he take the handful - Initially, when he takes the handful from this vessel, is it not heaped, and we require taking the handful from within the vessel? For anything that requires a vessel, only its interior is considered [the] vessel.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:5:2.hebrew: טפופה - פישל"א, שאינה גדושה. וכשקומץ מתוך כלי, קמץ באמצעיתו; וכשמחזיר, הרי קומץ בגודשת כלי, כדמפרש בסמוך:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:5:2.english: Full to the brim - [In Old French: *fisselle*], which is not heaped. And when he takes the handful from within the vessel, he took the handful from its middle; and when he returns [it], behold, the handful is in the heaped portion of the vessel, as [the Gemara] explains immediately following.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:6:1.hebrew: וקפריך דהא כי קמץ עבד גומא - וכי מהדר לקומץ בגומא, הוה ליה תוך כלי:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:6:1.english: And [the Gemara] objects that when he took the handful, he made a cavity - And when he returns the handful into the cavity, it is inside the vessel.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:6:2.hebrew: ומשני כי מהדר ליה אדופניתא דמנא - בצדי הכלי אצל גומא החזירו, והוי כגודש הכלי; ונייד למנא, ונפיל קומץ ממילא לגומא, כדי שיהא ראוי לקמיצת כהן. וכיון דממילא נפל למנא, נעשה כמי שהחזירו הקוף, ולא מקדש ליה כלי. ואע"ג דכלי שרת מקדשין שלא מדעת — הני מילי כי מהדר ליה איהו ממש; אדעתא דלא ליקדוש, מקדש ליה (האי) לכלי שמחזירו בהן, שמונח על גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:6:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: When he returns it to the wall of the vessel - He returned it onto the side of the vessel near the cavity, and it is [considered] like the heap of the vessel; and he shakes the vessel, and the handful falls by itself into the cavity, so that it will be fit for the taking of the handful by a priest. And since it fell into the vessel by itself, it is considered as though a monkey returned it, and the vessel does not sanctify it. And even though service vessels sanctify [even] without intent, this applies only when he himself actually returns it; [for then, even if done] with the intention that it not become sanctified, (this) vessel in which he returns it to them [the remnants], which is resting on the ground, sanctifies it.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:7:1.hebrew: קומצין - קומץ מכלי שעל גבי קרקע, וה"נ (מקדשין) קומץ מהבלול שעל גבי קרקע:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:7:1.english: One removes a handful - One removes a handful from a vessel that is on the ground, and here too, (one sanctifies) he removes a handful from the mixed [offering] that is on the ground.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:7:2.hebrew: דאיבעיא לן - כלומר, לחברינו איבעיא הך בעיא, דרב נחמן בעי מאבימי, וכדמפרש:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:7:2.english: That was raised before us - That is to say, to our colleagues was this dilemma raised, which Rav Naḥman asked of Avimi, and as [the Gemara] explains.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:8:2.hebrew: בלעי מאבימי - בלעתי מאבימי, כלומר שהיה מנדה אותו:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:8:2.english: I absorbed from Avimi - I absorbed from Avimi, that is to say, that he would place him under a ban.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:8:3.hebrew: עלה דהא שמעתא - במס' ערכין, דתנא חדא: שום היתומים ל' יום, ותניא אידך: ששים, ומתרץ לה אבימי: בא להכריז רצופין — כל ימות השבת — מכריז ל' יום:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:8:3.english: Regarding this teaching - In Tractate Arakhin, where one [baraita] taught: "The appraisal of orphans' [property] is thirty days," and another [baraita] taught: "Sixty [days]"; and Avimi resolves it: [If the court] comes to announce consecutively — [meaning on] all the days of the week — it announces for thirty days.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:8:4.hebrew: בא להכריז שני וחמישי - מכריז עד ס' יום, מיום שמתחיל עד יום שפוסק, דהיינו י"ח ימי הכרזה בס' יום, ומכריז: "מי יקנה נכסי יתומים הללו?", כדי שימכרו ביוקר. והיה רב חסדא משבח התירוץ ומבזי אבימי, אלמא רב חסדא תלמיד דאבימי הוה:
Rashi on Menachot 7a:8:4.english: [If one] comes to announce on Monday and Thursday - One announces for up to sixty days, from the day that one begins until the day that one ceases, which is eighteen days of proclamation within sixty days. And one proclaims: "Who will buy these orphans' property?" so that it will be sold for a high price. And Rav Chisda would praise the resolution and disparage Avimi, which shows that Rav Chisda was a student of Avimi.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:9:1.english: Avimi, tractate Menachot was uprooted for him - It was forgotten by him.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:9:2.english: And let him send to him - To Rav Chisda, that he should come to him.

Rashi on Menachot 7a:9:3.english: The matter is assisted - Because of [the dictum:] "I labored and found" (Megillah 6b).

Tosafot on Menachot 7a:10:1.hebrew: אמר ליה מכלי זה - למאי דמסיק דמגבה ליה כהן, יש לתמוה: מאי חידוש השיבו מכלי זה? ושמא אשמעינן, אע"פ שלא נמשח, שעבודתו מחנכת. א"נ, של עץ היה, כרבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, דאמר בפרק החליל (סוכה דף נ:) דעושין כלי שרת של עץ:
Tosafot on Menachot 7a:10:1.english: He said to him: From this vessel - According to that which is concluded, that a priest raises it [from the ground], one must wonder: What novelty did he answer him [by saying] "From this vessel"? And perhaps he was teaching us [that] even though it was not anointed, its service inaugurates it. Alternatively, it was [made] of wood, in accordance with Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Yehudah, who said in the chapter [entitled] "HeChalil" (Sukkah 50b) that one may make service vessels of wood.

Tosafot on Menachot 7a:1:1.hebrew: וכי מהדר ליה לקומץ לדוכתיה ליקדוש - ואע"פ ששירים מפסיקין בין קומץ לכלי, מין במינו אינו חוצץ:
Tosafot on Menachot 7a:1:1.english: And when he returns the handful to its place, let it become sanctified - And even though the remainder separates between the handful and the vessel, a substance of the same kind does not interpose (min be-mino eino chotzetz).

Tosafot on Menachot 7a:2:1.hebrew: א"ר יוחנן זאת אומרת כלי שרת אין מקדשין אלא מדעת - והא דפליגי חזקיה ורבי יוחנן לקמן בפרק התודה (מנחות דף עח:) [גבי תודה] ששחטה על שמונים חלות, וקאמר רבא דכולי עלמא כלי שרת מקדשין שלא מדעת — שאני התם, דמתוך שמקדש מדעת, מקדש נמי שלא מדעת. והא דמשמע בסוף לולב וערבה (סוכה דף נ.), דחזקיה סבר כלי שרת אין מקדשין שלא מדעת, גבי הא דתנן כמעשהו בחול כך מעשהו בשבת, ופריך בגמרא ונייתי במקודשת — התם אין כל המים ראוין להתקדש; אבל בהתודה, כיון דראוין לקדש, מקדש שלא מדעת. וצ"ע, דכיון דאין שיעור למים, הרי כולם ראוין להתקדש! ונראה, דכיון דשלא בזמנו הוא, אע"ג דכלי שרת מקדשין שלא בזמנו, כדמסקינן בסוף שתי הלחם (לקמן מנחות דף ק.), שלא מדעת מיהא אין מקדשין; ואע"ג דלילה אין מחוסר זמן:
Tosafot on Menachot 7a:2:1.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: That is to say, service vessels sanctify only with intent - And as for that dispute between Chizkiya and Rabbi Yochanan below in the chapter [entitled] "HaTodah" (Menachot 78b) [regarding a thanksgiving offering] that one slaughtered over eighty loaves, where Rava says that everyone agrees service vessels sanctify without intent — it is different there, for since it sanctifies with intent, it also sanctifies without intent. And as for that which is implied at the end of [the chapter] "Lulav Ve-Aravah" (Sukkah 50a), that Chizkiya holds service vessels do not sanctify without intent, regarding that which we learned: "As its procedure on a weekday, so was its procedure on Shabbat," and the Gemara challenges: "And let them bring [it] in a sanctified [vessel]?" — there, not all the water is fit to be sanctified; but in [the case of] the thanksgiving offering, since [the loaves] are fit to be sanctified, it sanctifies without intent. Yet this requires further study, because since there is no [fixed] measure for water, behold, all of it is fit to be sanctified! And it appears that since it is not in its proper time — even though service vessels sanctify [even] not in their proper time, as we conclude at the end of [the chapter] "Shtei HaLechem" (below, Menachot 100a) — at least without intent they do not sanctify; and [this is so] even though night is not [considered] lacking time.

Tosafot on Menachot 7a:3:1.hebrew: אין מקדשים ליקרב - הקשה ה"ר פטר, דלפי' הקונטרס בזבחים פרק המזבח מקדש (זבחים דף פז:), משמע שהשיבו ר' יוחנן דמקדשין לכתחילה ליקרב; דקאמר התם: בעי מיניה ר"ש בן לקיש מר' יוחנן, מהו שיקדשו את הפסולין? ופי' שם בקונטרס דלענין פדיון קא בעי, דאי מקדש הכלי — אין להם פדיון. א"ל: תניתוה, כשם שמזבח והכבש מקדשין את הראוי להם, כך כלי שרת מקדשין את הראוי להם; ואע"ג דמזבח וכבש איירי לענין דאם עלו לא ירדו, אייתי מינה ראיה לענין פדיון. א"ל: לכתחילה ליקרב קא מיבעיא לי! הא נמי תנינא: שקיבלו פסולין וזרקו את דמן, מאי לאו קבלו פסולין וזרקו פסולין? פי': הא זרקו כשרין, אף לכתחילה יעלו האברים; אלמא מקדשי לכתחילה ליקרב! ועוד קשה מהא דתנן התם: ואלו אם עלו לא ירדו: הלן, והיוצא, והטמא, והנשחט חוץ לזמנו וחוץ למקומו; וכולהו איירי בשנזרק הדם, כדמוכח בגמ' דקאמר עולא: אימורי קדשים קלים שהעלן לפני זריקת דמים לא ירדו, נעשו לחמו של מזבח; אמר ר' זירא: אף אנן נמי תנינא, שנשפך דמה ושיצא דמה חוץ לקלעים; ומה התם דאם בא לזרוק אינו זורק, אמרת אם עלו לא ירדו, הכא כו'. ומדלא מייתי מכל הני, ש"מ דאחר זריקה מיירי; ואפ"ה לכתחילה לא יעלו, אלמא אין מקדשין לכתחילה ליקרב האברים. ומיהו יש לדחות, דאכולהו קאי וזרקו את דמם. ועוד קשה, דבכמה דוכתי (פסחים דף טז:) אמרינן: נטמא הדם לא יזרוק, ואם זרק הורצה; ולמה לא יזרוק? הא כלי שרת מקדשין לכתחילה ליקרב! ובפ' שני שעירי (יומא דף סב.) אמרינן: נשפך הדם ימות המשתלח, מת המשתלח ישפך הדם; למה ישפך? וכן בדם פסולין, ישפך לאמה. ובפ' המנחות (לקמן מנחות ק:) תנן: נטמאו משהוקדשו בכלי אין להם פדיון, דמשמע: הא מיקרב לא קרב. ויש לדחות כל הני, בשעירה אחר כך לכלי חול. והא דשמעתין נמי יש ליישב לפי' הקונטרס: דהא דמשמע שהשיב לו אין מקדשין, היינו לפי שדוחה שם: לא, שקיבלו פסולים, א"נ וזורקן פסולין. ועוד קשה לפי' הקונטרס: דמדקאמר לכתחלה ליקרב קא מיבעיא ליה, משמע שגם רבי יוחנן היה יודע דליקרב קמיבעיא ליה, אלא שהיה סבור דמבעיא ליה בדיעבד, ולא מיירי כלל לענין פדיון. ולפר"ת: דמבעיא ליה אם מקדשין הפסולין לענין דאם עלו לא ירדו; דאע"ג דאי לאו כלי היה מזבח מקדשם, השתא דאיכא כלי גרע, שמפסיק בין הפסול למזבח. ומסיק דלכתחילה ליקרב מיבעיא ליה: אם קידשו הקומץ פסול בכלי, אם מעליהו; דדילמא כשם שהמזבח מקדש דלא ירד, כך כלי מקדש דיעלה. ופריך: דהא נמי תנינא, שקיבלו פסולים וזרקו, דמשמע זרקו דיעבד, אבל לכתחילה לא יזרוקו; והא דקאמר מאי לאו קיבלו פסולין וזרקו פסולין, לאו מלשון פסולין דייק, אלא המשנה קא מסיים, ופירושא דמתני' כך הוא. תדע, דהא ר"ש בן לקיש דדחי, בפסולין נמי מוקי לה; מכלל שלא דקדק רבי יוחנן בפסולין:
Tosafot on Menachot 7a:3:1.english: They do not sanctify [them] to be sacrificed - Rabbi Peter raised a difficulty: For according to Rashi's explanation in *Zevachim*, chapter *HaMizbe'ach Mekaddesh* (Zevachim 87b), it implies that Rabbi Yochanan replied to him that they sanctify [them] *ab initio* to be sacrificed; as [the Gemara] says there: Reish Lakish inquired of Rabbi Yochanan: What is [the halakha as to] whether they [service vessels] sanctify disqualified items? And Rashi explained there that he was asking with regard to redemption, for if the vessel sanctifies [them], they cannot be redeemed [with money]. He [Rabbi Yochanan] said to him: You have learned it: "Just as the altar and the ramp sanctify that which is suited to them, so too service vessels sanctify that which is suited to them." And even though the altar and the ramp deal with [the rule] that if they ascended they do not descend, he brought a proof from it regarding redemption. He [Reish Lakish] said to him: I was asking [whether they sanctify them] to be sacrificed *ab initio*! [Rabbi Yochanan replied:] This too we have learned: "[An offering whose blood] unfit [priests] received and sprinkled their blood [if it ascended it does not descend]"; what, is it not [referring to where] unfit [priests] received and unfit [priests] sprinkled? Meaning: but if fit [priests] sprinkled, even *ab initio* the limbs may ascend! Thus [it implies that] they sanctify [them] *ab initio* to be sacrificed! And furthermore, a difficulty arises from that which we learned there: "And these, if they ascended, do not descend: that which was left overnight, that which went out, that which became ritually impure, and that which was slaughtered outside its proper time or outside its proper place"; and all of them deal with [cases] where the blood was sprinkled, as is proven in the Gemara where Ulla said: "The sacrificial portions (eimurim) of offerings of lesser sanctity that one brought up [onto the altar] prior to the sprinkling of the blood do not descend, [because] they have become the food of the altar." Rabbi Zeira said: We too have learned: "[Offerings] whose blood was spilled, or whose blood went out beyond the hangings [if their meat ascended, it does not descend]"; and if there, where if he comes to sprinkle he may not sprinkle, you said if they ascended they do not descend, here, etc. And since he did not bring proof from all those [other cases], learn from this that they deal with [cases] after sprinkling; and even so, *ab initio* they may not ascend! This proves that they [service vessels] do not sanctify the limbs to be sacrificed *ab initio*! However, this can be dismissed [by arguing] that "and [unfit priests] sprinkled their blood" applies to all of them. And furthermore, a difficulty arises, for in several places (Pesachim 16b) we say: If the blood became ritually impure, he may not sprinkle [it], but if he sprinkled, it was accepted; and why should he not sprinkle [it]? Shouldn't service vessels sanctify [it] *ab initio* to be sacrificed? And in chapter *Shenei Se'irei* (Yoma 62a) we say: If the blood was spilled, the scapegoat shall die; if the scapegoat died, the blood shall be spilled; why should it be spilled? And likewise regarding the blood of disqualified [offerings], it shall be spilled into the canal. And in chapter *HaMenachot* (below, Menachot 100b) we learned: If they became ritually impure after they were sanctified in a vessel, they have no redemption; which implies: but being sacrificed, they are not sacrificed! And all of these can be dismissed [by answering that each case refers to] where he afterwards poured it into a non-sacred vessel. And that of our sugya here can also be resolved according to Rashi's explanation: For that which implies that he answered him "they do not sanctify" is because there he rejects [it by saying]: "No, [it is a case] where unfit [priests] received, or alternatively where their sprinkling was [performed by] unfit [priests]." And furthermore, a difficulty arises against Rashi's explanation: For since he said: "I was asking [whether it may be sacrificed] *ab initio*," this implies that Rabbi Yochanan also knew that he was asking regarding [whether it may be] sacrificed, but rather he thought that he was asking regarding *post facto*, and it was not dealing at all with the matter of redemption. And according to Rabbeinu Tam's explanation: [Originally,] he was asking whether they [service vessels] sanctify disqualified [items] with regard to [the rule] that if they ascended they do not descend; for even though, were it not for the vessel, the altar would have sanctified them, now that there is a vessel, is it worse, since it intervenes between the disqualified item and the altar? And he concludes [i.e., clarifies] that he was asking [whether they sanctify] to be sacrificed *ab initio*: if they sanctified a disqualified handful in a vessel, whether he may bring it up [onto the altar *ab initio*]; for perhaps just as the altar sanctifies [items placed on it] so that they do not descend, so too a vessel sanctifies [items placed in it] so that they may ascend! And he [Rabbi Yochanan] objects: This too we have learned: "[An offering whose blood] unfit [priests] received and sprinkled [if it ascended it does not descend]," which implies: [only if] they sprinkled *post facto*, but *ab initio* they shall not sprinkle! And that which he [Rabbi Yochanan] says: "What, is it not [referring to where] unfit [priests] received and unfit [priests] sprinkled?" He was not inferring from the wording of "unfit [priests]," but rather he was completing the mishna, and such is the interpretation of the mishna. You should know [that this is so], for Reish Lakish, who rejects [Rabbi Yochanan's proof], also establishes it with unfit [priests]; from which it follows that Rabbi Yochanan was not making a precise inference from [the word] "unfit [priests]."
